description: Licence to manufacture defence items listed in IDRA First Schedule/notified list
applies_when: Applies to private manufacturers of defence items
frequency_or_trigger: One-time application; validity extendable; commence production within stipulated period
form_or_filing: Form on DPIIT/DDP portal (Defence Industrial Licence application)
acts_rules: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act 1951; Arms Act 1959
obligation_register: Manufacturing without a valid defence industrial licence, or contravention of licence conditions, is punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both, under s.24 IDRA 1951; the licence itself can also be suspended/cancelled. Liable: Licence-holder company and officer in charge. Basis: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act 1951 s.24. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, courtkutchehry.com]

description: Seek extension of validity/commencement of production under defence industrial licence
applies_when: Licensee unable to start production in validity period
form_or_filing: Extension request on DPIIT e-Biz portal
acts_rules: IDRA 1951; Press Note/Defence Industrial Licensing policy
obligation_register: Failure to commence production within the licence's validity period without obtaining an extension can result in lapse/cancellation of the licence under IDRA 1951; general contravention of the Act is punishable under s.24 with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both. Liable: Licence-holder company and officer in charge. Basis: IDRA 1951 s.24. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, courtkutchehry.com]

description: Report production/capacity of licensed defence items
form_or_filing: Return prescribed by DPIIT/DDP (format Needs manual check)
obligation_register: Failure to file the mandatory annual production returns is a contravention under IDRA 1951, punishable under s.24 with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both, and may attract licence cancellation. Liable: Licence-holder company and officer in charge. Basis: IDRA 1951 s.24. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, courtkutchehry.com]

description: Licence to manufacture arms and ammunition
form_or_filing: Form under Arms Rules 2016 via MHA licensing portal
obligation_register: Manufacturing arms/ammunition without a licence (contravention of s.5) is punishable under s.25 Arms Act 1959 with imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and fine (higher penalties, up to life imprisonment, apply for prohibited arms under s.7/s.25). Liable: Manufacturer/company and responsible officers. Basis: Arms Act 1959 s.25 (r/w s.5). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, blog.ipleaders.in]

Selling or dealing in arms/ammunition without a dealer's licence (contravention of s.5) is punishable under s.25 Arms Act 1959 with imprisonment of 3 to 7 years and fine (up to life imprisonment for prohibited arms/ammunition). Liable: Dealer/company and licence holder. Basis: Arms Act 1959 s.25. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, blog.ipleaders.in]

Possessing or using arms after the licence has lapsed without renewal amounts to unlicensed possession, punishable under the Arms Act 1959 (imprisonment/fine per s.25 or the residual offence under s.30, depending on the category of arms); the licence can also be refused renewal/revoked. Liable: Licence-holder/company. Basis: Arms Act 1959 s.25/s.30. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, blog.ipleaders.in]

description: Maintain register of receipts, sales, stock
obligation_register: Failure to maintain the prescribed stock/sale register under the Arms Rules 2016 is an offence under the Arms Act 1959's residual penalty provision (s.30 - fine/imprisonment) and can result in suspension of the licence. Liable: Licence-holder/company. Basis: Arms Act 1959 s.30; Arms Rules 2016. [Knowledge-based]

description: Permission for import/export of arms and ammunition
acts_rules: Arms Act 1959; Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act 1992
obligation_register: Import/export of arms without the requisite permission attracts penalty under both the Arms Act 1959 (s.25 - imprisonment 3-7 years) and the FT(D&R) Act 1992 s.11(2) (monetary penalty of the higher of Rs 10,000 or 5x the value of goods, plus confiscation; imprisonment for specified/WMD-category goods under the WMD Act 2005). Liable: Importer/exporter company and officers. Basis: Arms Act 1959 s.25; FT(D&R) Act 1992 s.11. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, taxtmi.com]

compliance_name: Defence Procurement Manual/DAP compliance for bids
description: Follow eligibility, trial, QA and integrity terms in MoD procurement
form_or_filing: Bid documents; Integrity Pact under Defence Acquisition Procedure
acts_rules: Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 (currently in force); draft DAP 2026 released 10-Feb-2026 for stakeholder consultation, expected effective 1-Apr-2026 - final notification not confirmed as of Sep-2026
obligation_register: DAP 2020 is a government procurement policy, not a statute; non-compliance with bid/contract conditions leads to administrative consequences - bid disqualification, forfeiture of bid/performance security, blacklisting, and contract termination - rather than a statutory penalty. Liable: Bidder/vendor company. Basis: Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 (policy); no independent statutory penalty identified. [Knowledge-based]

description: Discharge offset obligations (min 30% for contracts above Rs 2,000 crore) via eligible offset
form_or_filing: Offset Contract; Offset Monitoring; Offset Guidelines under DAP
acts_rules: DAP 2020 Chapter/Appendix on offsets [Scheme/Policy, not a statute]; draft DAP 2026 (released Feb 2026) proposes revised offset framework - finalisation not confirmed as of Sep-2026
obligation_register: Non-discharge of the defence offset obligation under DAP 2020 (policy, not statute) leads to encashment of the offset bank guarantee/liquidated damages and can affect eligibility for future contracts; there is no separate statutory penal provision. Liable: Vendor/offset obligor company. Basis: DAP 2020 offset guidelines (policy). [Knowledge-based]

description: Submit claims with documentary evidence for offset credit
acts_rules: DAP 2020 offset guidelines [Scheme/Policy, not a statute]; superseding draft DAP 2026 (Feb 2026) pending finalisation as of Sep-2026
obligation_register: Failure to submit periodic offset claims on schedule can lead to forfeiture of offset credits and encashment of the associated bank guarantee under the DAP 2020 offset guidelines; this is an administrative/contractual consequence, not an independent statutory penalty. Liable: Vendor/offset obligor company. Basis: DAP 2020 offset guidelines (policy). [Knowledge-based]

description: Certify Indian Content for DAP categories (Buy Indian-IDDM etc.)
form_or_filing: IC certificate by statutory auditor/cost accountant
acts_rules: DAP 2020; Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017
obligation_register: Incorrect/false indigenous-content certification can lead to disqualification from the tender, forfeiture of bid/performance security, blacklisting, and recovery of undue benefit under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017/DAP 2020, besides possible action for misrepresentation. Liable: Bidder company and authorised signatory. Basis: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017; DAP 2020 (policy). [Knowledge-based]

description: Authorisation for export of dual-use/military items
form_or_filing: SCOMET licence application on DGFT portal (ANF-2O; ANF-2M is for import of restricted items, not export)
acts_rules: Foreign Trade (Development and Regulation) Act 1992; ITC(HS) Appendix 3 SCOMET list; FTP 2023
obligation_register: Exporting SCOMET items without the requisite authorisation is punishable under s.11(2) FT(D&R) Act 1992 with a monetary penalty (higher of Rs 10,000 or 5x the value of goods) and confiscation; for WMD-related items, criminal prosecution/imprisonment applies under the WMD Act 2005. Liable: Exporter company and responsible officers. Basis: FT(D&R) Act 1992 s.11. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, taxtmi.com]

form_or_filing: EUC documents per Handbook of Procedures
obligation_register: Furnishing a false SCOMET end-use certificate or diverting goods from the declared end-use is a contravention under s.11(2) FT(D&R) Act 1992 (monetary penalty as above) and, for WMD-category items, criminal prosecution under the WMD Act 2005; the export authorisation/IEC can also be suspended. Liable: Exporter company/authorised signatory. Basis: FT(D&R) Act 1992 s.11. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, taxtmi.com]

frequency_or_trigger: Before commencing; renewal per licence term
form_or_filing: Form LE-1 / prescribed forms on PESO portal
obligation_register: Manufacturing explosives without, or in contravention of, a licence is punishable under s.9B Explosives Act 1884 with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both. Liable: Licence-holder/company and person in charge of manufacture. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9B. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

form_or_filing: Form LE-3/LE-4 etc under Explosives Rules 2008 (exact form Needs manual check)
obligation_register: Storing explosives without, or contrary to, licence conditions is punishable under s.9B (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 5,000) or, where it amounts to unlicensed possession/use, under s.9C (imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs 3,000). Liable: Licence-holder/company. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9B/s.9C. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

Transporting explosives without a valid transport licence is punishable under s.9C Explosives Act 1884 with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs 3,000, or both. Liable: Licence-holder/transporter company. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9C. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

Importing explosives without a valid import licence is punishable under s.9B Explosives Act 1884 with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both, besides confiscation of the consignment. Liable: Importer/licence-holder company. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9B. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

Failure to report an explosives accident is punishable with fine up to Rs 500; if the accident caused loss of human life, the punishment is imprisonment up to 3 months or fine, or both, under the Explosives Act 1884/Rules. Liable: Licence-holder/occupier of the premises. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 (accident-reporting provision). [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

description: Meet milestones and IP terms for iDEX grants
acts_rules: iDEX scheme guidelines (administrative) [Scheme/Policy, not a statute]
obligation_register: iDEX/DIO guidelines are an administrative scheme, not a statute; non-compliance with grant/contract terms leads to termination of the contract, recovery of disbursed funds, and disqualification from future iDEX rounds, rather than a statutory penalty. Liable: Grantee start-up/company. Basis: iDEX scheme guidelines (policy). [Knowledge-based]

DGQA vendor registration/approval is an administrative quality-assurance process, not backed by a distinct penal statute; non-compliance results in suspension/withdrawal of vendor registration and rejection of supplies rather than a statutory fine. Liable: Vendor/manufacturer company. Basis: DGQA policy (administrative). [Knowledge-based]

DGAQA/CEMILAC aeronautical quality approval is an administrative process; non-compliance leads to suspension/withdrawal of the approval and inability to supply aeronautical products/services, rather than a statutory monetary penalty. Liable: Manufacturer/design agency company. Basis: Administrative approval process (CEMILAC/DGAQA). [Knowledge-based]

description: Airworthiness certification for military aircraft systems
obligation_register: Non-compliance with CEMILAC design-certification requirements can lead to withdrawal/suspension of type/design approval and disqualification from future DRDO/MoD contracts; this is an administrative sanction, not a distinct statutory penalty. Liable: Design agency/manufacturer company. Basis: DRDO/CEMILAC administrative certification process. [Knowledge-based]

description: Safeguard classified information; security clearance of staff
obligation_register: Unauthorised communication or wrongful use of official secrets relating to a defence establishment is punishable under s.3 Official Secrets Act 1923 with imprisonment up to 14 years (defence-related matters) or up to 3 years (other cases); unauthorised possession/retention of official documents is punishable under s.5 with imprisonment up to 3 years, fine, or both. Liable: Individual employee/officer. Basis: Official Secrets Act 1923 s.3, s.5. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, drishtiias.com]

description: Facility security clearance for classified projects
acts_rules: Official Secrets Act 1923; MoD security manual
obligation_register: Breach of facility security-clearance conditions can attract prosecution under s.3/s.5 Official Secrets Act 1923 (imprisonment up to 14 years or 3 years respectively) besides revocation of the facility's security clearance by MoD. Liable: Company/facility and responsible officers. Basis: Official Secrets Act 1923 s.3, s.5; MoD security manual. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, drishtiias.com]

description: Government approval for FDI beyond 74% (automatic up to 74%) or where access to modern technology
form_or_filing: FDI Policy; FIFP/DPIIT approval via Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal
acts_rules: FDI Policy (Consolidated); FEMA Non-Debt Instruments Rules 2019
obligation_register: Undertaking FDI in defence beyond permitted sectoral caps/route, or in breach of conditions, is a contravention under s.13(1) FEMA 1999, attracting a penalty up to thrice the sum involved (or up to Rs 2 lakh if not quantifiable), plus Rs 5,000/day for continuing default; compounding is available. Liable: Indian company receiving FDI and its officers. Basis: FEMA 1999 s.13(1); NDI Rules 2019. [Search-confirmed - taxmann.com, enterslice.com]

compliance_name: FEMA FC-GPR reporting for defence FDI
description: File FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment
obligation_register: Delayed/non-filing of FC-GPR is a contravention under s.13(1) FEMA 1999; RBI levies a Late Submission Fee and, on adjudication, a penalty up to thrice the amount involved (or Rs 2 lakh if not quantifiable) plus Rs 5,000/day continuing default can also be imposed. Liable: Indian company (FDI recipient) and its officers. Basis: FEMA 1999 s.13(1); NDI Rules 2019. [Search-confirmed - taxmann.com, enterslice.com]

description: Import authorisation for restricted defence items
obligation_register: Importing defence items without, or contrary to, an import licence is a contravention under s.11(2) FT(D&R) Act 1992, punishable with a monetary penalty (higher of Rs 10,000 or 5x the value of goods) and confiscation of goods; SCOMET/WMD-related imports also draw criminal prosecution. Liable: Importer company and officers. Basis: FT(D&R) Act 1992 s.11. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, taxtmi.com]

description: Compliance with DPE guidelines: MoU, corporate governance, CSR
form_or_filing: DPE Guidelines on Corporate Governance for CPSEs 2010
obligation_register: DPE guidelines are administrative instructions for CPSEs, not an independent penal statute; non-compliance is addressed through performance-rating downgrades and administrative action by the administrative Ministry, while related statutory obligations (audit, disclosures) fall under the Companies Act 2013. Liable: DPSU/company and its Board/officers. Basis: DPE Guidelines 2010 (administrative); Companies Act 2013. [Knowledge-based]

description: Annual Memorandum of Understanding with MoD
obligation_register: The MoU with the Ministry is a policy/performance-management tool; non-achievement of MoU targets affects the DPSU's performance rating and incentives rather than triggering a statutory penalty. Liable: DPSU company/Board. Basis: DPE MoU Guidelines (administrative policy). [Knowledge-based]

description: Facilitate CAG audit and annual report laying
form_or_filing: CAG audit under Section 143(5) Companies Act
obligation_register: An auditor who contravenes ss.139, 144 or 145 Companies Act 2013 is punishable under s.147 with fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh; if the contravention is knowing/wilful to deceive, imprisonment up to 1 year and fine of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 25 lakh apply, with liability to refund fees/damages; CAG's statutory audit and its placement before Parliament are governed by the CAG's (DPC) Act 1971. Liable: Company officers/auditor. Basis: Companies Act 2013 s.147 (r/w ss.139, 143); CAG's (DPC) Act 1971. [Search-confirmed - ibclaw.in, corporatelawreporter.com]

acts_rules: Drone Rules 2021 (confirmed still in force); draft Civil Drone (Promotion and Regulation) Bill 2025 (released 16-Sep-2025) not yet enacted
obligation_register: Operating a drone without registration/remote pilot certificate under the Drone Rules 2021 is punishable under s.10/11A Aircraft Act 1934 (savings continue pending new BVA Rules) with a civil penalty up to Rs 1 lakh under the Rules, and up to Rs 1 crore under the Act's rule-making power for serious contraventions; the UIN/certificate can be suspended or cancelled. Liable: Drone operator and owning company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Drone Rules 2021. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, civilaviation.gov.in]

description: AOC to operate air transport services
form_or_filing: DGCA application under Aircraft Rules 1937 (Aircraft Rules 2025 status Needs manual check)
acts_rules: Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 (in force 1 Jan 2025, S.O. 5646(E); replaced Aircraft Act 1934); Aircraft Rules 1937 pending new Bharatiya Vayuyan Rules (draft 2025)
obligation_register: Operating air transport services without a valid Air Operator Certificate/permit is punishable under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 with imprisonment up to 2 years (up to 3 years for aggravated offences such as dangerous flying) and/or fine up to Rs 1 crore, or a civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore imposed by a designated officer; DGCA can also suspend/cancel the AOC. Liable: Operator company and its accountable manager/directors. Basis: Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 (penalty provisions). [Search-confirmed - prsindia.org, indiacode.nic.in]

description: Aircraft Act 1934 replaced by Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024; commencement/rules to be verified
acts_rules: Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 (in force 1 Jan 2025, S.O. 5646(E); replaced Aircraft Act 1934)
obligation_register: As the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024 replaces the Aircraft Act 1934 (in force 1-Jan-2025), failure to transition licences/permits/approvals is dealt with under the same penalty regime as the new Act: imprisonment up to 2-3 years and/or fine up to Rs 1 crore, or a civil/rule-contravention penalty up to Rs 1 crore. Liable: Licence/permit-holder company. Basis: Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam 2024. [Search-confirmed - prsindia.org, indiacode.nic.in]

description: Renew CoA / ARC for each aircraft
obligation_register: Operating an aircraft without a valid Certificate of Airworthiness contravenes the Aircraft Rules 1937 and is punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 1,000 (general rule contravention), or a civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore under the Act's rule-making power; DGCA can also ground the aircraft. Liable: Aircraft owner/operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Aircraft Rules 1937. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

form_or_filing: Form to DGCA (CAR Section 2 Series F Part I)
obligation_register: Operating an unregistered aircraft contravenes the Aircraft Rules 1937 and is punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 1,000, or a civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore; the aircraft can also be grounded/de-registered. Liable: Owner/operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

Operating as an unapproved maintenance organisation or breaching CAR-145 conditions is punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore) and can lead to suspension/revocation of the AMO approval by DGCA. Liable: AMO company and accountable manager. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; CAR-145. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

description: Ensure pilots' licences, ratings, medicals valid
obligation_register: Flying, or permitting a flight, without a valid flight-crew licence or medical certificate contravenes the Aircraft Rules 1937 and is punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore); the licence/medical certificate can also be suspended. Liable: Pilot/crew member and operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

Failure to implement/report under the Safety Management System requirement is a rule contravention under the Aircraft Rules 1937/CAR, punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore) besides regulatory action on the operator's certificate. Liable: Operator company/accountable manager. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

form_or_filing: Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules 2017
acts_rules: Aircraft Act 1934; Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules 2017
obligation_register: Failure to report an aircraft accident/incident under the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules 2017 is punishable under s.10/11A Aircraft Act 1934 with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs 1,000, or a civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore; it can also invite suspension of the AOC. Liable: Operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10/11A; AAIB Rules 2017. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

form_or_filing: Aircraft (Demolition of Obstructions) Rules; Aerodrome licence Form
obligation_register: Operating an aerodrome without a valid licence contravenes the Aircraft Rules 1937 and is punishable under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore); DGCA can also suspend/cancel the aerodrome licence. Liable: Aerodrome licensee/operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

acts_rules: Aircraft (Demolition of Obstructions Caused by Buildings and Trees etc.) Rules 1994
obligation_register: Erecting a building/structure without the mandatory height NOC violates the Aircraft (Demolition of Obstructions Caused by Buildings and Trees etc.) Rules 1994, and can result in demolition of the offending structure and prosecution under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore). Liable: Owner/developer of the structure. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Demolition of Obstructions Rules 1994. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, advocatekhoj.com]

acts_rules: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act 2008; AAI Act 1994
obligation_register: Wilful non-compliance with an order of the Appellate Tribunal is punishable under s.37, and non-compliance with orders/directions of AERA/Tribunal under ss.38-39 AERA Act 2008 (fine, quantum not independently confirmed); offences by companies are separately covered under s.40. Liable: Airport operator/airline company and officer in default. Basis: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act 2008 ss.37-40. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tdsat.gov.in]

Non-compliance with an approved aviation security programme under the Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023 is punishable under s.10/11A Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore) and can result in suspension of the security clearance/programme approval by BCAS. Liable: Airport/airline operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, civilaviation.gov.in]

Operating as a regulated agent/known consignor without or in breach of BCAS approval contravenes the Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023, leading to withdrawal of approval and prosecution under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934 (imprisonment up to 3 months/fine up to Rs 1,000, or civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore). Liable: Regulated agent/consignor company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, civilaviation.gov.in]

Allowing staff to access airside without a valid Airport Entry Permit breaches the Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023, leading to permit cancellation, denial of airside access, and possible prosecution under s.10 Aircraft Act 1934. Liable: Employer/airport operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Aircraft (Security) Rules 2023. [Knowledge-based]

Penalty provision not independently confirmed - ground handling is regulated through administrative policy (MoCA/DGCA Ground Handling Policy) rather than a distinct statute; consult legal counsel for the applicable consequence. [Needs manual check]

description: Remote pilot certificate and UAS operator permit
acts_rules: Drone Rules 2021 (confirmed still in force); draft Civil Drone (Promotion and Regulation) Bill 2025 not yet enacted
obligation_register: Operating a drone without registration/remote pilot certificate under the Drone Rules 2021 is punishable under s.10/11A Aircraft Act 1934 (savings continue pending new BVA Rules) with a civil penalty up to Rs 1 lakh under the Rules, and up to Rs 1 crore under the Act's rule-making power for serious contraventions; the UIN/certificate can be suspended or cancelled. Liable: Drone operator/remote pilot and owning company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; Drone Rules 2021. [Search-confirmed - aaib.gov.in, civilaviation.gov.in]

compliance_name: Passenger charter compliance (CAR Section 3 Series M)
form_or_filing: CAR Section 3 Series M Part IV
obligation_register: Non-compliance with passenger-charter obligations (CAR Section 3 Series M - denied boarding, delay/cancellation compensation) can result in DGCA-imposed civil penalty up to Rs 1 crore under the Aircraft Act 1934/BVA 2024 rule-making power, plus directions to pay passenger compensation; it may also affect the airline's licence conditions. Liable: Airline/operator company. Basis: Aircraft Act 1934 s.10; CAR Section 3 Series M. [Knowledge-based]

description: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 assented 18 Aug 2025; replaces 1958 Act from date of notification; status of commencement and rules needs checking
obligation_register: The Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (in force from 15-Mar-2026) re-enacts the offences-and-penalties framework of the MSA 1958; failure to transition to the new registration/certification regime by the effective date exposes the vessel/company to detention and the penalty prescribed for the specific contravention, though the exact re-numbered section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Shipowner/company. Basis: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (offences and penalties provisions). [Needs manual check]

description: Act commenced 10 Sept 2025 replacing Indian Bills of Lading Act 1856
obligation_register: Non-compliance with the Bills of Lading Act 2025 (transfer of contractual rights of suit) does not carry a criminal penalty; the consequence is civil liability - the carrier/consignee remains liable in contract for loss or damage, enforceable through an ordinary civil suit. Liable: Carrier/shipper company. Basis: Bills of Lading Act 2025 (re-enactment of the Indian Bills of Lading Act 1856). [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 2025
description: Replaces Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 1925; applies to carriage under bills of lading
acts_rules: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 2025
obligation_register: The Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 2025 (re-enacting COGSA 1925/Hague Rules) fixes carrier liability limits and defences for cargo loss/damage rather than prescribing a penal offence; non-compliance exposes the carrier to civil damages claims up to the statutory package limitation, without a separate criminal penalty. Liable: Carrier/shipping company. Basis: Carriage of Goods by Sea Act 2025. [Knowledge-based]

acts_rules: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (in force from 15-Mar-2026, replacing Merchant Shipping Act 1958 except Part XIV)
obligation_register: Operating an Indian ship without valid registration is an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act's offences chapter (historically Part XVI, MSA 1958, re-enacted in MSA 2025 effective 15-Mar-2026); the vessel is liable to detention and the owner to fine/prosecution, though the exact re-numbered MSA 2025 section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Shipowner/registered-owner company. Basis: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (offences and penalties, Part XVI equivalent). [Needs manual check]

description: Load line, safety, radio, pollution certificates
acts_rules: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (in force from 15-Mar-2026, replacing Merchant Shipping Act 1958 except Part XIV); SOLAS, MARPOL
obligation_register: Operating a ship without valid statutory survey/SOLAS certificates is an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act's penalty provisions, exposing the ship to detention under Port State/Flag State Control and the owner to fine/prosecution; the exact MSA 2025 section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Shipowner/company (certificate holder). Basis: Merchant Shipping Act 2025; SOLAS/MARPOL. [Needs manual check]

description: DOC and SMC; ship security certificates
acts_rules: Merchant Shipping Act; SOLAS Ch IX
obligation_register: Failure to hold a valid ISM Document of Compliance/Safety Management Certificate or ISPS Ship/Port Security Certificate can lead to detention of the vessel by Port State Control and prosecution under the Merchant Shipping Act's penalty provisions; the exact MSA 2025 section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Shipowner/DOC-holder company. Basis: Merchant Shipping Act; SOLAS Ch. IX/XI-2 (ISM/ISPS Codes). [Needs manual check]

frequency_or_trigger: Licence renewal (5 yr) with annual compliance
acts_rules: Merchant Shipping (Recruitment and Placement of Seafarers) Rules 2016
obligation_register: Operating as a recruitment and placement service provider without a valid RPSL licence, or in breach of its conditions, can lead to suspension or cancellation of the RPSL licence by DG Shipping (after an opportunity of hearing); the Merchant Shipping Act's penal provisions for operating without the requisite licence may also apply. Liable: RPSL agency/company. Basis: Merchant Shipping (Recruitment and Placement of Seafarers) Rules 2016; Merchant Shipping Act. [Search-confirmed - legalbabu.com, indianemployees.com]

Non-compliance with Maritime Labour Convention requirements can result in denial/withdrawal of the Maritime Labour Certificate/DMLC, detention of the ship under Port State Control, and prosecution under the Merchant Shipping (MLC) Rules 2016/Merchant Shipping Act penalty provisions. Liable: Shipowner/company. Basis: Merchant Shipping (Maritime Labour Convention) Rules 2016; Merchant Shipping Act. [Knowledge-based]

compliance_name: Coastal vessels permits (licence to non-Indian ships)
description: General trading licence for coastal shipping
obligation_register: Operating a non-Indian ship in the coasting trade without the requisite licence is an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act's coasting-trade provisions, exposing the ship to seizure/detention and the operator to fine/prosecution; the exact MSA 2025 section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Ship operator/charterer company. Basis: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (coasting-trade provisions). [Needs manual check]

acts_rules: Merchant Shipping Act 2025 (in force from 15-Mar-2026); MARPOL
obligation_register: Operating without a valid International Oil Pollution Prevention Certificate, or discharging oil in contravention of MARPOL, is an offence under the Merchant Shipping Act's pollution-prevention provisions, exposing the shipowner to fine/prosecution and the vessel to detention; the exact MSA 2025 section was not independently confirmed. Liable: Shipowner/company. Basis: Merchant Shipping Act 2025; MARPOL Annex I. [Needs manual check]

compliance_name: Port Trust tariff & Major Port Authorities Act
description: Compliance with port tariff and licences
obligation_register: General contravention of the Major Port Authorities Act 2021 or of rules/regulations/orders (including tariff directions) is punishable with fine up to Rs 1 lakh under s.62; offences committed by companies are separately dealt with under s.63. Liable: Port user/company and officer in default. Basis: Major Port Authorities Act 2021 s.62, s.63. [Search-confirmed - mumbaiport.gov.in, ksandk.com]

acts_rules: Indian Ports Act 1908 repealed; replaced by Indian Ports Act 2025 (notified 21-Aug-2025, in force)
obligation_register: Serious offences under Schedule 1 of the Indian Ports Act 2025 (e.g., endangering vessel safety, disturbing the port waterbed without permission) are punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs 1 lakh, or both, tried by a Judicial Magistrate; operational lapses under Schedule 2 (e.g., commencing port operations without notification) draw a monetary penalty imposed administratively by the Conservator. Liable: Port operator/vessel owner and officer in default. Basis: Indian Ports Act 2025, Schedule 1/Schedule 2 offences. [Search-confirmed - prsindia.org, lexology.com]

description: Replacement statute for Indian Ports Act 1908
acts_rules: Indian Ports Act 2025 (notified 21-Aug-2025, in force, repealing Indian Ports Act 1908)
obligation_register: Serious offences under Schedule 1 of the Indian Ports Act 2025 draw imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine up to Rs 1 lakh (tried by a Judicial Magistrate First Class); operational lapses under Schedule 2 draw administrative monetary penalties imposed by the Conservator, and wilful non-compliance with a Dispute Resolution Committee order attracts a penalty up to Rs 1 lakh plus Rs 1,000/day continuing default. Liable: Port authority/operator company and officer in default. Basis: Indian Ports Act 2025 Schedule 1/2; DRC penalty clause. [Search-confirmed - prsindia.org, lexology.com]

description: Registration and certificate of survey for inland vessels
obligation_register: Operating a mechanically propelled inland vessel without a valid certificate of survey or certificate of registration is punishable with a penalty of up to Rs 10,000 for a first offence and up to Rs 25,000 for a subsequent offence under Chapter XVI, Inland Vessels Act 2021; more serious safety contraventions can draw imprisonment up to 3 years. Liable: Vessel owner/operator company. Basis: Inland Vessels Act 2021, Chapter XVI (Offences and Penalties). [Search-confirmed - prsindia.org, indiacode.nic.in]

acts_rules: Inland Waterways Authority of India Act 1985
obligation_register: Penalty provision not independently confirmed - non-payment of IWAI navigation/terminal charges or contravention of IWAI directions is generally addressed through recovery proceedings/denial of navigation rights, but the specific penal section of the IWAI Act 1985 was not independently confirmed; consult legal counsel. [Needs manual check]

description: Compliance with Customs Act and CBLR
obligation_register: Goods dealt with in violation of the Customs Act are liable to confiscation under s.111, and any person concerned in such dealing is liable to penalty under s.112 - up to the value of the goods (or Rs 5,000, whichever is greater) for prohibited goods, or up to the duty evaded (or Rs 5,000, whichever is greater) for dutiable goods; serious cases attract criminal prosecution under s.135, and a Customs Broker's licence can be revoked under the CBLR. Liable: Customs Broker/bonded-warehouse licensee company. Basis: Customs Act 1962 ss.111, 112, 135. [Search-confirmed - taxguru.in, indiankanoon.org]

description: Registration of vendors of railway items
obligation_register: RDSO vendor registration/approval is an administrative process under Railway Board policy, not a distinct penal statute; non-compliance leads to suspension/de-listing from the RDSO approved-vendor list and disqualification from tenders rather than a statutory fine. Liable: Vendor/manufacturer company. Basis: RDSO vendor-approval policy (administrative); Railways Act 1989 (general framework). [Knowledge-based]

Railways contractor registration/enlistment is governed by Railway Board's administrative contract-management policy; non-compliance results in de-registration, blacklisting from future tenders, and forfeiture of earnest money/security deposit, rather than a distinct statutory penalty under the Railways Act 1989. Liable: Contractor company. Basis: Railway Board contractor policy (administrative); Railways Act 1989. [Knowledge-based]

description: Compliance with labour laws for contractors
form_or_filing: Labour law returns [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 subsumed)
obligation_register: Contravention of contract-labour welfare/registration provisions is punishable under the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 - a penalty of Rs 50,000 to Rs 1 lakh for prohibited/unregistered employment of contract labour, and a general penalty of Rs 2-3 lakh under s.94 where no specific penalty is prescribed; the principal employer (Railway Administration) can also be held liable for contract-labour welfare. Liable: Contractor/principal employer and company officers. Basis: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020, s.94 and contract-labour provisions. [Search-confirmed - lexology.com, pib.gov.in]

Failure to furnish or maintain the performance guarantee/security deposit is a breach of contract under the Indian Contract Act 1872; the consequence is forfeiture of the guarantee/deposit and/or termination of the contract, not a distinct statutory penalty. Liable: Contractor company. Basis: Indian Contract Act 1872 (contractual forfeiture); tender/contract conditions. [Knowledge-based]

Breach of a private-siding or wagon-investment agreement with the Railway Administration is enforced through contractual remedies (termination, recovery of dues, forfeiture of siding facility) under the Railways Act 1989/agreement terms, rather than a distinct statutory penalty. Liable: Siding owner/company. Basis: Railways Act 1989 (siding provisions); private siding agreement. [Knowledge-based]

description: CRS sanction for new lines/rolling stock
acts_rules: Railways Act 1989; Metro Railways (Operation and Maintenance) Act 2002
obligation_register: Opening a railway/Metro line or altering level crossings/bridges without the sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety is an offence under the Railways Act 1989 penal chapter (Chapter XV), attracting fine and, where it endangers safety, imprisonment; the exact section for want of CRS sanction was not independently confirmed. Liable: Railway administration/Metro operator company. Basis: Railways Act 1989 Chapter XV (Penalties and Offences); Metro Railways (O&M) Act 2002. [Needs manual check]

description: Generation does not need licence but requires CEA concurrence for hydro; captive registration
obligation_register: Contravention of the generation-related provisions/directions of the appropriate Commission is punishable under s.142 Electricity Act 2003 with fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day for continuing contravention; wilful non-compliance with a Commission/Appellate Tribunal order draws imprisonment up to 3 years or fine, or both, under s.146. Liable: Generating company and officer in default. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 ss.142, 146. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

form_or_filing: CERC (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Transmission Licence) Regulations
obligation_register: Operating as a transmission licensee in breach of licence conditions or Commission directions is punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and, for wilful non-compliance with orders, under s.146 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine, or both); CERC can also revoke the licence under s.19. Liable: Transmission licensee company and officer in default. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 ss.142, 146, 19. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

Operating as a distribution licensee in breach of licence conditions or Commission directions is punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and, for wilful non-compliance with orders, under s.146 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine, or both); SERC can also revoke the licence under s.19. Liable: Distribution licensee company and officer in default. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 ss.142, 146, 19. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

Operating as a trading licensee in breach of licence conditions or Commission directions is punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and, for wilful non-compliance with orders, under s.146 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine, or both); CERC can also revoke the licence under s.19. Liable: Trading licensee company and officer in default. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 ss.142, 146, 19. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

acts_rules: Electricity Act 2003 s.42; Electricity (Promoting Renewable Energy Through Green Energy Open Access) Rules 2022
obligation_register: Failure to comply with open-access conditions/directions of CERC/SERC/SLDC is punishable under s.142 Electricity Act 2003 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and, for wilful non-compliance with an order, under s.146 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine, or both). Liable: Open-access consumer/generator company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 ss.142, 146. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

description: Annual proof of 26% ownership and 51% consumption
acts_rules: Electricity Act 2003 s.9; Electricity Rules 2005 r.3
obligation_register: Loss of captive-generation status for non-compliance with the 26% equity/51% self-consumption norms under r.3 Electricity Rules 2005 results in the plant being treated as an ordinary generating company/licensee (denial of captive tariff/open-access benefits) rather than a criminal penalty; general non-compliance with Commission directions is separately punishable under s.142 Electricity Act 2003. Liable: Captive generating plant/company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.9, s.142; Electricity Rules 2005 r.3. [Knowledge-based]

form_or_filing: CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations 2023
obligation_register: Contravention of CEA safety regulations for works, plant and lines issued under s.53 Electricity Act 2003 is punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and can lead to disconnection/prohibition of the unsafe installation by the Electrical Inspector. Liable: Owner/operator company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.53, s.142. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

Commissioning an electrical installation without the approval of the Chief Electrical Inspector under CEA Safety Regulations 2023 is punishable under s.142 Electricity Act 2003 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and can result in the Inspector prohibiting use of the installation. Liable: Installation owner/company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.142; CEA Safety Regulations 2023. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

form_or_filing: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 - Renewable Consumption Obligation; MoP orders (status Needs manual check)
acts_rules: Electricity Act 2003 s.86(1)(e); Energy Conservation Act 2001
obligation_register: Shortfall in Renewable Purchase Obligation is enforced by the SERC under s.86(1)(e) Electricity Act 2003, typically through a forced-procurement direction/deposit into a fund; continuing non-compliance with the SERC's direction is punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing). Liable: Obligated entity (DISCOM/open-access consumer) company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.86(1)(e), s.142. [Knowledge-based]

acts_rules: CERC (Terms and Conditions for recognition and issuance of RECs) Regulations
obligation_register: Non-compliance with REC Regulations (e.g., double-counting, non-redemption) can lead to suspension/cancellation of REC accreditation by CERC/Grid-India, and is enforceable as a contravention of Commission regulations under s.142 Electricity Act 2003 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing). Liable: Generator/registered entity company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.142; CERC REC Regulations. [Knowledge-based]

description: Designated consumers submit Form-A and Form-1; achieve SEC targets
obligation_register: Failure of a designated consumer to meet the notified energy-consumption norms under the PAT scheme attracts a penalty under s.26 Energy Conservation Act 2001 of up to Rs 10 lakh, with an additional Rs 10,000/day for continuing failure, adjudicated by the State Commission's adjudicating officer; a shortfall can also be met by purchase of Energy Saving Certificates. Liable: Designated consumer company. Basis: Energy Conservation Act 2001 s.26 (r/w ss.14, 15). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, lexology.com]

compliance_name: Energy audit and energy manager appointment
description: Appoint certified energy manager; mandatory energy audit
obligation_register: Failure to conduct the mandated energy audit or appoint a certified energy manager under ss.14/15 Energy Conservation Act 2001 attracts a penalty under s.26 of up to Rs 10,000 for each failure, with an additional Rs 1,000/day for continuing failure. Liable: Designated consumer company. Basis: Energy Conservation Act 2001 s.26 (r/w ss.14, 15). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, lexology.com]

acts_rules: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022; Needs manual check [Scheme/Policy, not a statute]
obligation_register: Penalty provision not independently confirmed - the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 is still being operationalised through BEE/MoP regulations; consult legal counsel for the currently applicable penalty mechanism. [Needs manual check]

Non-compliance with the Grid Code specified by CERC under s.79 Electricity Act 2003 is punishable as a contravention under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing) and can result in disconnection from the grid by Grid-India/RLDC. Liable: Grid user (generator/DISCOM) company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.79, s.142. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

Failure to file the annual tariff true-up petition under s.62 Electricity Act 2003 is a contravention of Commission directions/regulations, punishable under s.142 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing), and can result in the Commission determining tariff suo motu or disallowing cost recovery. Liable: Licensee (generation/transmission/distribution) company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.62, s.142. [Search-confirmed - lawgist.in, indianconstitution.in]

description: Registration, ALMM listing for solar modules
acts_rules: Approved List of Models and Manufacturers orders
obligation_register: Using modules/manufacturers not on the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers is not an offence under a specific statute; the consequence is that the project becomes ineligible for the government scheme/subsidy/PPA benefit tied to ALMM-listed equipment (administrative consequence). Liable: Project developer company. Basis: MNRE ALMM Order (administrative policy). [Knowledge-based]

Non-compliance with net-metering connection standards under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules 2020 can lead to the DISCOM refusing/disconnecting the net-metering connection; persistent non-compliance with Commission regulations is separately punishable under s.142 Electricity Act 2003 (fine up to Rs 1 lakh, plus Rs 6,000/day continuing). Liable: Consumer/rooftop-solar installer company. Basis: Electricity Act 2003 s.142; Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules 2020. [Knowledge-based]

Obstructing an officer or the State/National Dam Safety Organisation in the discharge of duties under the Dam Safety Act 2021 is punishable under s.41 with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine, or both; non-compliance with safety directions that causes loss of life carries enhanced imprisonment up to 2 years. Liable: Dam owner/company and officer in default. Basis: Dam Safety Act 2021 s.41 (r/w s.35, obligations of dam owner). [Search-confirmed - advocatekhoj.com, cmr.edu.in]

acts_rules: SHANTI Act 2025 (repealed Atomic Energy Act 1962 and Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010)
obligation_register: Under the SHANTI Act 2025, operating without or in breach of an AERB licence attracts a graded monetary penalty (up to Rs 1 crore for severe breaches) imposed by an Adjudicating Officer under s.70 (appealable to APTEL), with imprisonment reserved for grave offences/criminal negligence; AERB can also suspend the licence or order a shutdown. Liable: Licensee/operator company (and, for grave offences, responsible individuals). Basis: SHANTI Act 2025 s.70 (adjudication of penalties). [Search-confirmed - jsalaw.com, lexology.com]

description: Authorisation for City Gas Distribution / pipelines
acts_rules: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board Act 2006
obligation_register: Laying/operating a city gas distribution network without valid PNGRB authorisation is punishable under s.28 PNGRB Act 2006 with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both, plus an additional fine up to Rs 10 lakh/day for continuing contravention. Liable: Entity/company operating the network. Basis: PNGRB Act 2006 s.28. [Search-confirmed - pngrb.gov.in, blog.ipleaders.in]

description: Registration for marketing of petroleum products
obligation_register: Marketing notified petroleum, LPG or CNG without valid PNGRB registration is punishable under s.28 PNGRB Act 2006 with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both, plus an additional fine up to Rs 10 lakh/day for continuing contravention. Liable: Marketing entity/company. Basis: PNGRB Act 2006 s.28. [Search-confirmed - pngrb.gov.in, blog.ipleaders.in]

acts_rules: PNGRB Act 2006; Integrity Management System Regulations 2012
obligation_register: Failure to conduct the mandated Integrity Management System audit under the IMS Regulations 2012 is enforced as a contravention of PNGRB regulations, attracting action under s.28 PNGRB Act 2006 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both) and can lead to suspension of the authorisation. Liable: Authorised entity/company. Basis: PNGRB Act 2006 s.28; Integrity Management System Regulations 2012. [Knowledge-based]

Non-compliance with PNGRB's technical standards and safety (T4S) requirements is enforceable under s.28 PNGRB Act 2006 (imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 25 crore, or both) and can lead to suspension/revocation of the authorisation. Liable: Authorised entity/company. Basis: PNGRB Act 2006 s.28. [Knowledge-based]

description: Licence for storing petroleum Class A/B/C
obligation_register: Storing/importing petroleum without a valid licence under the Petroleum Rules 2002 is an offence under the Petroleum Act 1934's general offence provision (s.23); a pending 2026 amendment bill proposes raising unlicensed-activity penalties to imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 25 crore, but this is not yet enacted as of Sep-2026. Liable: Licence-holder/storage company. Basis: Petroleum Act 1934 s.23; Petroleum Rules 2002. [Search-confirmed - ianslive.in, issehs.com]

Transporting petroleum by road without a valid transport-vehicle licence under the Petroleum Rules 2002 is an offence under the Petroleum Act 1934's general offence provision (s.23); the pending 2026 amendment bill proposes enhanced penalties (imprisonment up to 3 years/fine up to Rs 25 crore) not yet enacted. Liable: Transporter/licence-holder company. Basis: Petroleum Act 1934 s.23; Petroleum Rules 2002. [Search-confirmed - ianslive.in, issehs.com]

Manufacturing, filling or possessing gas cylinders without the requisite licence under the Gas Cylinders Rules 2016 is enforced through the Explosives Act 1884 (s.9B: imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 5,000, or both, for manufacture/import contraventions; s.9C: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs 3,000 for possession/use contraventions). Liable: Licence-holder/company. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9B/s.9C; Gas Cylinders Rules 2016. [Search-confirmed - indiacode.nic.in, tilakmarg.com]

acts_rules: Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules 2016
obligation_register: Operating a static/mobile pressure vessel without the requisite PESO approval under the SMPV(U) Rules 2016 is enforced through the Explosives Act 1884 penalty framework (s.9B/s.9C - imprisonment up to 2-3 years or fine up to Rs 3,000-5,000, or both), since the Rules are issued under that Act. Liable: Vessel owner/company. Basis: Explosives Act 1884 s.9B/s.9C; SMPV(U) Rules 2016. [Knowledge-based]

acts_rules: Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act 1948; Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules 1959
obligation_register: Rules under the Act may prescribe imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs.1,000 (Rs.100/day for continuing offence) for contravention; recent amendment shifts to civil/monetary penalties by an Adjudicating Authority. Liable: Licensee/lessee and, for company offences, officers in default. Basis: Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Act 1948, s.9 (rules); Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules 1959. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

description: Right of user in land compliance
acts_rules: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act 1962
obligation_register: Wilful obstruction/damage to pipeline works punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine or both; wilful unauthorised connection/damage to a laid pipeline punishable with rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years plus fine. Liable: Person committing the act (contractor/company personnel). Basis: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act 1962, s.15. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

Cess is levied as a duty of excise; delayed/non-payment attracts recovery with interest and enforcement akin to Central Excise Act recovery provisions (no separate imprisonment clause located). Liable: Crude oil producer/company. Basis: Oil Industries (Development) Act 1974, s.15 read with Central Excise Act 1944 recovery provisions. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

compliance_name: Motor Spirit and HSD (Regulation of Supply, Distribution) Order compliance
obligation_register: Contravention of orders under s.3 (other than clauses h/i) punishable with imprisonment of 3 months to 7 years and fine; repeat conviction bars trading in the commodity for a minimum 6 months, with forfeiture of goods/vehicle. Liable: Dealer/company and officers in default. Basis: Essential Commodities Act 1955, s.7 (MS&HSD Order made thereunder). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

description: Amended OFRD Act enacted 2025; commencement/rules to be checked
obligation_register: The 2025 amendment overhauls the criminal-penalty regime of the parent 1948 Act, replacing imprisonment with monetary penalties imposed by a designated Adjudicating Authority for contraventions. Liable: Licensee/lessee. Basis: Oilfields (Regulation and Development) Amendment Act 2025 (amending s.9 of the 1948 Act). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

form_or_filing: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (Regulation of Supply and Distribution) Order 2000
obligation_register: Same as MS&HSD Order: contravention of the Control Order punishable with imprisonment of 3 months to 7 years and fine under s.7; repeat offence carries trading debarment and forfeiture. Liable: Distributor/dealer and officers in default. Basis: Essential Commodities Act 1955, s.7 (LPG Control Order made thereunder). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

acts_rules: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act 1957
obligation_register: Unauthorised mining (contravening s.4/4(1A)) punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to Rs.5 lakh per hectare of area; rule contraventions punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs.5 lakh, plus continuing fine up to Rs.50,000/day. Liable: Lessee/licensee and person conducting mining operations. Basis: Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act 1957, s.21. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

description: Approved mining plan and progressive closure
obligation_register: Contravention of MCDR (e.g., mining plan violations) is a 'major violation' punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs.5 lakh or both (2021 amendment rationalised major/minor violations; minor violations now fine-only). Liable: Mine owner/lessee/manager. Basis: MCDR 2017, rr.22-23 read with MMDR Act 1957 s.23C/s.21. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

Same MCDR penalty regime as IND-MIN-02 - failure to file statutory returns is a minor violation attracting fine per Schedule III (major violations up to 2 yrs imprisonment/Rs.5 lakh fine). Liable: Mine owner/lessee/manager. Basis: MCDR 2017, r.45 penalty provisions. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]
Same MCDR penalty regime as IND-MIN-02/03 for annual return default. Liable: Mine owner/lessee/manager. Basis: MCDR 2017 penalty provisions. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

Non-payment/short payment of DMF contribution attracts recovery as arrears of land revenue and interest; failure to remit treated as breach of lease conditions risking lease termination. Liable: Mining lease holder. Basis: MMDR Act 1957, s.9B. [Knowledge-based]

Non-payment of NMET contribution attracts recovery as arrears of land revenue/lease breach; similar consequences to royalty default including risk of lease suspension. Liable: Mining lease holder. Basis: MMDR Act 1957, s.9C. [Knowledge-based]

Non-payment of royalty is recoverable as arrears of land revenue with interest; persistent default can lead to lease termination under s.4A. Liable: Lessee. Basis: MMDR Act 1957, s.9 read with s.25. [Knowledge-based]

form_or_filing: Mines Rules [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Mines Act, 1952 subsumed)
obligation_register: OSH Code prescribes fine between Rs.2 lakh and Rs.3 lakh for contraventions with no specified penalty; specific defaults (e.g. medical report) fine up to Rs.10,000; repeat offences within 5 years attract imprisonment up to 3 months and/or higher fine, or both. Liable: Employer/mine owner and occupier. Basis: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020, Ch.XI penalty provisions (erstwhile Mines Act 1952 s.72B-73 subsumed). [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

acts_rules: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Mines Act, 1952 subsumed); Coal Mines Regulations 2017
obligation_register: Same OSH Code penalty regime (fine Rs.2-3 lakh; imprisonment on repeat contravention) applies to failure to appoint statutory mine manager/officials. Liable: Mine owner/manager. Basis: OSH Code 2020, Ch.XI; Coal Mines Regulations 2017. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

form_or_filing: Form per regulation [legacy form name; Code-era format to confirm]
acts_rules: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 (in force 21 Nov 2025; erstwhile Mines Act, 1952 subsumed)
obligation_register: Failure to notify accident/dangerous occurrence is an offence under the OSH Code attracting fine (Rs.2-3 lakh range) and, on repeat, imprisonment; serious safety violations causing death/injury can trigger higher penalties under Ch.XI. Liable: Mine owner/manager/occupier. Basis: OSH Code 2020, Ch.XI. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, prsindia.org]

compliance_name: Environmental clearance and Forest clearance for mine
acts_rules: Environment Protection Act 1986; EIA Notification 2006; Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam 1980
obligation_register: Contravention of EC/FC conditions is punishable under EP Act s.15 with imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 7 years for continuing default beyond 1 year) and fine up to Rs.1 lakh with Rs.5,000/day continuing fine; Forest Act violations attract separate penalties under the Van Adhiniyam. Liable: Project proponent/company and officers in default. Basis: Environment (Protection) Act 1986, s.15; EIA Notification 2006; Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam 1980. [Search-confirmed - indiankanoon.org, pib.gov.in]

Operating without/violating CTE-CTO conditions: under Water Act, failure to comply with directions attracts imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Rs.10,000 (s.41); contravening s.24 (discharge without consent) draws imprisonment 1.5-6 years and fine (s.43); Air Act carries a parallel penalty regime under s.37 (imprisonment 1.5-6 years and fine, extendable to 7 years for continuing contravention).
